title: Conveyor belt list: an endless list from ten elements, drawn round two rollers
blurb: A virtualised list with no end as a conveyor belt. Rows come up round the bottom roller and go over the top one, and ten real elements are reused for every row. Each row has a checkbox and a button that take taps while the belt moves.
question: Can an endless list be drawn as a conveyor belt, with rows that come up round a roller and go over another, from a fixed number of real elements that still take taps while they move?
result: Yes in Chromium 157. Ten elements show any row, row 1,000,000 included. Each element is drawn once when its picture changes and copied to a plain canvas, the belt is drawn from the copy in slices, and updateElementGeometry() puts each row's hit box where the row is. A touch drag of 190 px drew 53 frames with 6 element draws.
